messages:
maria: Heads up — tenant metadata backfill wave hitting prod-us-east-1 just spiked replica lag to ~120s at epoch 42. Seeing lots of lock waits, pausing the next waves for now. Need rollback/throttle plan.
kevin: Which backfill job id and command? I can throttle if we need a quick change.
kevin: command I ran last night for the wave: `scripts/backfill/tenant_meta_backfill --epoch=42 --batch-size=10000 --parallel=12`
jamal: Confirming logs: got repeated `lock timeout: 10s` on writes to tenant_meta_index. CPU ok, but queueing on primary. Metrics: write latency jump at 15:02 UTC. Suggest immediate batch-size drop to 2k and enable epoch-level throttle.
sophia: If primary lock contention persists we should stop the active backfill instead of running smaller waves — we risk cascading replica lag. We can mark remaining tenants for async resubmit.
maria: Agreed. Plan A = pause + throttle + resume. Plan B = abort waves and reschedule off-peak. Thoughts on rapid rollback vs graceful pause?
priya: deploybot reports a canary failure for the schema-sidecar on canary-03 around the same time (lock timeout in logs). Not a full DDL rollback yet but a warning.
deploybot: [automated] Canary 03 failed healthcheck at 2026-03-07T15:04:12Z — exit code 1; reason: lock timeout encountered while applying prebackfill hook. See https://deployments.internal/canary/1769994999
migration-bot: [alert] Active backfill job 4583 detected >100s replication lag on replica r-us-east-3. Suggested action: pause-wave OR reduce concurrency.
kevin: Immediate actions I'll take now: 1) Pause remaining waves in orchestrator. 2) Patch the backfill to `--batch-size=2000 --parallel=4`. 3) Add `--epoch-throttle=0.25` env on job. Executing step 1 now.
maria: OK pausing orchestrator. @kevin ping when patch ready so we can resume a single canary wave.
jamal: Quick safe abort snippet if we need to fully cancel: 
```
# cancel backlog for wave 42
orchestrator cancel-wave --id=42 --reason="replica-lag-spike"
kubectl delete job backfill-4583
```
sophia: If we abort, we must also update release-notes and notify CS — some tenants expect completion window today. Add a short rollback blurb in release notes and open a postmortem ticket.
priya: I'll draft the blurb once we decide abort vs throttle. For now I'm pushing the canary logs to the release channel.
kevin: Patch uploaded: pushed branch `backfill/throttle-epoch-42` that reduces batch size + throttles. I'm running a single resubmit to canary wave 42a with `--parallel=2`.
kevin: resubmit kicked off. Monitoring replica lag...
maria: Seeing lag drop to ~30s on canary replica after 60s — good sign. If stable for 10m we can continue slow waves.
jamal: Agreed. Continue with rate-limited waves: schedule next 3 waves with 5m gaps and the patched params. If any wave exceeds 60s lag we stop and escalate.
sophia: Can we add a temporary feature flag to redirect heavy tenant reads to read-through cache for 24h? Might reduce pressure.
kevin: Added `tenant_backfill_rate_limiter=true` feature flag in featuregate service. Toggle set to gradual rollout.
maria: Nice. Final checklist before resuming: 1) Pause orchestrator — done. 2) Patch job — done. 3) Run single canary — done and stable. 4) Update release notes/CS — pending (priya). 5) Document rollback steps in the thread (jamal) — done.
priya: Drafted release-note snippet: "Backfill for tenant metadata experienced transient lock contention during epoch 42 — waves paused and throttled. Resumed under rate-limited config; monitoring. No customer-facing downtime expected. Postmortem pending." Will post in releases channel after approval.
maria: OK let's proceed with slow waves. If any escalation, we'll follow abort snippet above and open urgent pg-scale rollback. Thanks team :thumbsup:
kevin: ack :thumbsup:
migration-bot: [info] Wave 42a completed canary run at 2026-03-07T15:12:58Z. Replica lag steady. Continuing scheduled slow waves.
priya: Noted — posting release note and tagging CS now.
sophia: I'll open the postmortem ticket and add the lock traces.
maria: Closing thread — will reopen if anything regresses.
